mechanism: Building permits lead housing starts and construction activity and are one of the earliest cyclical movers (a Conference Board leading-index component). Permits growing faster than a year earlier mark housing and its supply chain expanding (risk-on); shrinking permits are an early sign of a cyclical slowdown.
key_finding: As known at the time (real-time PERMIT vintages), the rule selected on in-sample data uses zscore_60m / T_z_0 at L10 (IS Sharpe 0.83); held-out OOS Sharpe 0.44 versus buy-and-hold SPY 0.96.
caveats: The strategy is search-selected and needs a frozen-rule holdout confirmation.
Building permits are revised after the first print, so the as-known-at-the-time and revised tracks differ through revisions as well as release timing.
Lead estimates rest on a limited number of housing cycles in the sample.
The test window was seen by the previously published runs, so it is not a frozen hold-out.
narrative_summary: Building permits year-over-year growth (PERMIT) is tested as a procyclical housing-cycle overlay for SPY. The level of permits is a separate pair (permit_spy).

data_provenance.source: FRED / ALFRED (U.S. Census Bureau / HUD, new residential construction)
